transcript.text: Hello! My name is Daniel, and I'm a student. Today, I'm going to tell you about my daily routine.

On weekdays, I usually wake up at seven o'clock. I don't like getting up early, especially when the weather is cold, but I have to get ready for school. First, I wash my face and brush my teeth. Then I get dressed and go to the kitchen. My mother usually prepares breakfast for the family. I normally have eggs, bread, and tea. Sometimes I eat cereal with milk if I don't have much time.

I leave home at about half past seven. My school is not very far away, so I usually walk there. It takes around fifteen minutes. I like walking because I can get some fresh air before my lessons start. If it rains, my father sometimes drives me to school.

Lessons begin at eight o'clock. I study different subjects, including English, mathematics, history, and science. English is my favourite subject because I enjoy learning new words and speaking with my classmates. Mathematics is a little more difficult for me, but I try to practise it every day.

We have a short break at ten thirty. I usually talk to my friends or buy something small to eat. Our lunch break is at twelve thirty. I often bring a sandwich and some fruit from home, but sometimes I eat lunch in the school cafeteria.

School finishes at two thirty. When I get home, I have lunch if I'm hungry and then take a short rest. After that, I do my homework. I usually spend about one hour on it, but some days I need more time.

In the evening, I like listening to music, watching videos, or playing computer games. I also help my parents with small jobs around the house. For example, I sometimes wash the dishes or tidy my room.

We usually have dinner together at seven thirty. After dinner, I prepare my school bag and choose my clothes for the next day. I don't want to do these things in the morning because I'm often in a hurry.
Before going to bed, I sometimes read a few pages of a book. I usually go to bed at ten thirty. I know that getting enough sleep is important, so I try not to stay up late.
That's my usual weekday. My weekends are quite different because I don't have to go to school.
Hi, Jack! How was your weekend?
It was great, thanks. I spent most of it with my family. We had a small family lunch on Sunday.
That sounds nice. How many people are there in your family?
There are five of us: my parents, my older sister, my younger brother, and me. My grandparents live in another town, but they visit us quite often.
Do you get along well with your brother and sister?

Most of the time! My sister is twenty, so she's older than me by three years. She's quite responsible and always helps me with my studies. My younger brother is only eight. He's funny and energetic, but sometimes he makes a lot of noise.
I have a younger sister too. She's ten, and we share a bedroom. Sometimes we argue because she takes my things without asking.
I understand that! My brother sometimes uses my headphones. I tell him to ask me first, but he forgets.
What do your parents do?
My father is an engineer. He works in an office and usually comes home at six. My mother is a teacher. She works at a primary school not far from our house.
Does your mother help you with your homework?
Sometimes, especially with English. But my sister is better at mathematics, so I usually ask her for help with that subject.
What do you usually do together as a family?
We often have dinner together. At weekends, we sometimes watch a film or visit my grandparents. My father also enjoys cooking, so he prepares special meals on Sundays.
What did you do at your family lunch yesterday?
My grandmother made her famous chicken soup, and my father prepared a big dish of plov. We also had a salad and some fruit. After lunch, we sat in the garden and talked.
That sounds lovely. I don't see my grandparents very often because they live far away.
You should call them more often. My grandmother really enjoys talking on the phone. She always asks me about school and my friends.
You're right. I'll call them this evening.
That's a good idea. Family is important, even when everyone is busy.

title: Finding a New House
format: Conversation between a customer and an estate agent

transcript.text: Good morning. Welcome to Green Homes. How can I help you?
Good morning. I'm looking for a house to rent. My family and I want to move next month.
Of course. How many bedrooms do you need?
Three bedrooms would be perfect. We have two children, and they need their own space. We would also like a small garden.
I see. Do you have a monthly budget?
We'd prefer to pay around eight hundred dollars a month. We could pay a little more for the right house, but we don't want anything too expensive.

I have two possible houses. The first one is in the city centre. It has three bedrooms, a large kitchen, and a comfortable living room. There is a supermarket across the street, and the bus stop is only two minutes away.
That sounds convenient. Does it have a garden?
Unfortunately, no. It has a small balcony instead. The rent is seven hundred and fifty dollars per month.
Hmm. We really want a garden because our children enjoy playing outside. What about the second house?
The second house is in a quieter neighbourhood, about twenty minutes from the city centre by bus. It has three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and a lovely garden. There is also a small park nearby.
That sounds much better. Is there a supermarket in the area?
Yes. There is one about five minutes away on foot. There is also a primary school near the park.
Excellent. How much is the rent?
Eight hundred and twenty dollars per month. Water and heating are included, but electricity is not.
That's a little above our budget, but it might be possible. Is the house furnished?
It has a sofa, a dining table, and some kitchen cupboards. However, there are no beds or wardrobes.
That's fine. We have our own beds. Can we visit the house this week?
Certainly. I have an appointment available on Thursday at four in the afternoon.
Thursday at four works for me. I'll come with my wife.
Great. Could I have your phone number so I can confirm the appointment?
Of course. I'll give it to you now.

Hello, everyone! Today, we're going to talk about food around the world. Food is an important part of every culture. People in different countries eat different meals, use different ingredients, and have their own cooking traditions.

Let's start with Italy. Italian food is famous in many countries. Pizza and pasta are two of the most popular dishes. Italian people often use tomatoes, cheese, olive oil, and fresh vegetables. Many families enjoy eating together, especially at weekends. A traditional Italian meal can take quite a long time because people like talking while they eat.

Now, let's travel to Japan. Rice is an important part of Japanese food. Many people eat rice with fish, vegetables, and soup. Sushi is one of the most famous Japanese dishes. It usually contains rice and fish, although there are different types. Japanese meals are often simple and carefully prepared.

In Mexico, food is usually full of flavour. Tacos are very popular. People put meat, vegetables, cheese, or beans inside small tortillas. Some Mexican dishes are spicy because cooks use different kinds of peppers. However, not every Mexican meal is hot. There are also many sweet dishes and desserts.

Let's visit India. Indian food is known for its spices. People use ingredients such as rice, potatoes, tomatoes, and different spices. Curry is a popular dish, and there are many different versions. Some people eat meat, while others prefer vegetarian meals. In fact, vegetarian food is very common in many parts of India.

Finally, let's talk about Uzbekistan. Uzbek cuisine has a long history and many traditional dishes. Plov is probably the most famous one. It is usually made with rice, meat, carrots, onions, and oil. People often prepare it for family celebrations and special events. Other popular dishes include somsa, manti, and shashlik.
Although food is different around the world, it brings people together. Families share meals, friends meet at restaurants, and people celebrate important moments with special dishes.
So, next time you try food from another country, remember that you are also learning something about its culture. Thank you for listening!
Hi, Daniel! Are you busy this Saturday?
Not really. Why are you asking?
My cousin is visiting us this weekend. I want to show her around the city, but I don't know where to take her.
That's nice! What's her name?
Her name is Sophie. She's seventeen, and she's really interested in photography. She loves taking pictures of interesting buildings and beautiful places.
Then you should take her to the old part of the city. There are some beautiful historical buildings there. The streets are quite narrow, but they look amazing in photographs.
That's a good idea. Is there anything else we can do?
Well, there's a new art exhibition at the city museum. It opened last Monday. My sister went there yesterday, and she said it was really interesting.
Does it cost much?
No, the tickets are quite cheap. I think they're around five dollars for students. Adults pay eight dollars.
Perfect! What about lunch? I don't want to spend the whole day walking around without eating anything.
There's a small Italian restaurant near the museum. I went there with my family last month. The food was delicious, and the prices were reasonable.
Does it serve vegetarian food? Sophie doesn't eat meat.
Yes, they have several vegetarian dishes. My sister ordered a vegetable pizza, and she really enjoyed it.
Great. Maybe we can invite some other friends too.
Sure. What about Mark and Lisa? They usually have free time on Saturdays.
I'll send them a message tonight. By the way, what time should we meet?
How about nine thirty in the morning? We can meet in front of the central library.
Isn't that a little early? I usually wake up at nine on Saturdays!
Come on, Emma! We have a lot to see. But we can make it ten o'clock if you prefer.
Ten is much better. I'll probably take a taxi because the bus is always crowded in the morning.
I think I'll come by bicycle. The weather forecast says it will be sunny, so it should be a pleasant ride.
Excellent. I'll bring my camera, and Sophie can use my old phone to take pictures too.
Sounds like a plan! Don't forget to charge your camera tonight.
I won't. See you on Saturday!
See you!
Hey, Sam! I haven't seen you for a few days. How are things?
Pretty good, thanks. I've been quite busy recently. I've started going to a new sports club.
Really? What kind of sport do you do there?
I play basketball three times a week. I've always liked basketball, but I never had enough time to practise regularly.
That's great! Do you play with your school friends?
Sometimes. But the club has different groups. My group has twelve people, and most of them are around my age. Our coach is very friendly, but he expects us to work hard.
How long are your training sessions?
About ninety minutes. We usually start with some simple exercises to warm up. Then we practise passing, shooting, and working as a team. At the end, we play a short match.
That sounds fun. I used to play basketball when I was younger, but I stopped because I didn't have a good team.
You should join us! We need one more player for our Saturday group.
I'd love to, but I'm not very good at basketball anymore.
Don't worry about that. Nobody expects you to be perfect. The important thing is to practise and enjoy the game.
You're right. How much does the club cost?
It's thirty dollars a month. You can also pay for three months together, which is a little cheaper.
That's not too expensive. Do I need to bring anything?
Just sports clothes, comfortable trainers, and a bottle of water. They have basketballs at the club, so you don't need to buy one.
Nice. Where is it?
It's next to the city swimming pool, about ten minutes from the central bus station. You can take bus number six. It stops right outside the sports centre.
I know that area. What time do you train on Saturdays?
Our session starts at eleven in the morning. But I usually arrive fifteen minutes early because I like to get ready before training.
I think I'll come with you this Saturday. Can I watch first?
Of course! You can watch the first half, and then you can join us if you want.
Great. By the way, do you do any other activities?
I also go swimming on Sundays. It's a good way to relax after a busy week. I used to spend most of my weekends playing computer games, but now I prefer doing something active.
I should probably do the same. I spend too much time sitting at home.
You don't have to change everything at once. Just start with one activity you enjoy.
Good advice. I'll see you on Saturday, then.
See you! And don't forget your water bottle!
Good morning, students!
I have some important information about activities at our school next week. Please listen carefully and write down anything you need to remember.

First, let's talk about the school library. From Monday, the library will open at eight thirty in the morning instead of nine. It will close at four thirty in the afternoon. Students can borrow up to three books at a time. You can keep each book for two weeks. If you need more time, you can ask the librarian to extend the borrowing period.

Next, we are organising a school sports day on Wednesday. It will take place on the school playground, starting at ten o'clock. There will be several activities, including football, basketball, volleyball, and running competitions. Students who want to take part should give their names to their class teachers before Tuesday afternoon. Remember to wear comfortable sports clothes and bring a bottle of water.

Now, some information about the English club. We have decided to change the meeting day. The club usually meets on Thursday, but next week it will meet on Friday at three fifteen. The meeting will be in Room 12, not Room 8. We will watch a short film and discuss the characters and the story. You don't need to prepare anything before the meeting.

There is also a science exhibition in the main hall next Thursday. Students from different classes have prepared small projects about animals, plants, and the environment. The exhibition will open at nine in the morning and finish at one o'clock. You can visit it with your classmates during your free lesson. Please remember that food and drinks are not allowed in the exhibition area.

Finally, I want to remind everyone about the school trip. We are going to the history museum on Friday, the twenty-first of this month. The bus will leave from the school entrance at eight fifteen, so please arrive at least fifteen minutes early. The journey will take about forty minutes. You should bring a packed lunch, a notebook, and a pen. The school will pay for the bus, but students need to bring money for their museum tickets. The ticket costs four dollars.
If you have any questions about these activities, please speak to your class teacher. Thank you for listening, and have a good day!
Welcome to Teen Life. Today we're talking about hobbies. Our guest is Olivia Green. Olivia, could you spell your surname for our listeners?
Of course. Green. That's G-R-E-E-N.
Thank you. So, what do you enjoy doing in your free time?
Photography is my favourite hobby. I started two years ago, when my uncle gave me his old camera. I like taking pictures of nature, especially birds and flowers.
Where do you take your photos?
Usually in Maple Park, near my house. Maple. That's M-A-P-L-E. It has a lake and lots of tall trees. I go there on Saturday mornings, because it's quiet and there aren't many people.
Do you have another hobby?

Yes, I love baking with my grandmother. We usually make biscuits. She has an old notebook full of family recipes, and we try a new one every week. Last month, I made a chocolate cake for my best friend's birthday. It was a big surprise!
How do you find time for all this?
During the week, I do my homework first. Then I have some free time in the evening. At weekends, I have more time for my hobbies.
Do you have a goal for this year?

Yes! I'd like to enter a photography competition. It's for teenagers aged thirteen to seventeen, and you can send up to five photos. The last day to send them is the fifteenth of May. I don't expect to win, but I want to learn from the experience.
That sounds great. How can our listeners find out more?
They can call the competition office. The number is oh seven nine four, six two one, eight three zero.
Oh seven nine four, six two one, eight three zero?
Yes, that's right.
Thank you, Olivia, and good luck!
Good afternoon, and welcome to the shopping centre! How can I help you today?
Hi. I'm meeting my cousin here, but I can't find her.
No problem! What's her name? I can call her over the speakers.
Hannah Brooks.
Brooks? How do you spell that?
Brooks. That's B-R-O-O-K-S.
Great, thanks! Did she say where to meet?
She said near the bookshop.
The bookshop is on the second floor, next to the cinema. You can take the lift right behind you.
Thank you. I also need a present for my little brother. He's ten, and he loves building things.
Then you should try Toybox. That's T-O-Y-B-O-X. It's a toy shop near the main entrance. They have a great wooden building set for just eighteen dollars and fifty cents.
Perfect. Is there somewhere to eat?
Yes! The food court is near the car park entrance. There's a little café there that sells really good sandwiches.
And what time does the centre close today?
Today is Saturday, so we close at nine p.m. On Sundays, we close earlier.
Is there an ATM?
Yes, right next to the customer service desk.
OK. And what if I still can't find my cousin?
Just call us at the information desk. The number is oh two oh seven, four nine one, three five six.
Oh two oh seven, four nine one, three five six?
That's right!
One more thing. Can I get the present wrapped?
Of course! Gift wrapping is free at the customer service desk.
Wonderful. Thank you so much!
You're welcome. Have a great day!
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our city tour! My name is Peter Wilson, and I'll be your guide today. Wilson. That's W-I-L-S-O-N.

We're starting here in the main square, the biggest square in the city. Our first stop is the City Museum, just across the road. The building is very old. Before it was a museum, it was a school. The museum is closed on Mondays, so we're lucky it's Tuesday today! Inside, you can see old maps and photos of the city.

Next, we'll walk to Riverside Park. Riverside. That's R-I-V-E-R-S-I-D-E. The park is next to the river. It has a long walking path, two playgrounds and a small café. At the café, fresh juice costs three dollars, and it's really good!

After the park, we'll visit the market. It's famous for fresh fruit and vegetables. It's very busy on Saturday mornings, but today it will be quiet. Then, at half past twelve, we'll have lunch at a small restaurant near the market.

Our last stop is the City Library. It has three floors, and the top floor is a quiet study area. If you get lost, please meet us at the library entrance. You can also call me. My number is oh seven eight one, three five two, six four nine. That's oh seven eight one, three five two, six four nine.
Oh, and bring an umbrella. It might rain this afternoon. Enjoy the tour!
Hi! My name is Tom Fisher. Fisher. That's F-I-S-H-E-R. Today I'm going to tell you about the best holiday I've ever had.

Last summer, my family went to a small town in the mountains. We went by train. We left home very early, at a quarter to seven in the morning, and the journey took four hours. My uncle was waiting for us at the station.
We stayed in a small guesthouse with a beautiful garden. Our room had a balcony with a view of the mountains.
On the first evening, we ate at a local restaurant. I had vegetable soup and grilled chicken. My little sister had pasta.

The next morning, we went hiking with a guide. She showed us a safe path through the forest. We saw lots of birds and even a small fox! Later, we stopped at a waterfall and took photos. It was sunny in the morning, but in the afternoon it became cloudy and windy.
On the third day, we visited a farm. There were goats, sheep and chickens, and a friendly dog called Max. Max. That's M-A-X. He followed us everywhere and played with my sister.
The farmer told us that visitors should always phone first. His number is oh one two three, six four eight, five nine seven. That's oh one two three, six four eight, five nine seven.
We stayed for five days and came home on the fifteenth of July. I loved the mountain walk, but my sister says playing with Max was the best part!
Good morning, everyone. Today we're talking about our dreams for the future. Emma, would you like to start? First, please tell us your full name for the new class list.
Sure. I'm Emma Clarke. Clarke. That's C-L-A-R-K-E.
Thanks, Emma. So, what do you want to be?
I want to become a doctor, because I enjoy helping people. Biology is my favourite subject, but I need to improve my chemistry.
That's a great dream. Where would you like to study?
At Oakwood University. Oakwood. That's O-A-K-W-O-O-D. It has a very good medical school, and it's only an hour from my home.
Wonderful. And what about your friends? Do you know their dreams?
Yes! My best friend wants to be a computer programmer. She already makes small websites. And my brother wants to be a football coach, because he loves helping younger players.
Those are great goals. But remember, a dream needs a plan. You should choose small steps. For example, Emma, you could review science for thirty minutes a day.
Should we write our goals down?

Yes. Write one small goal for this month and one bigger goal for the next three years. Bring your plans to our next lesson on the twenty-second of November. We'll meet in Room fourteen. If you have any questions, call the school office. The number is oh one six one, four nine six, two oh three.
Oh one six one, four nine six, two oh three?
That's right.
Great. I'll talk to my parents about my plan tonight.
Welcome to Careers Today! My guest is a careers adviser, Lucy Foster. Lucy, can you spell your surname for us?
Of course. Foster. That's F-O-S-T-E-R.
Today we're talking about three different jobs. Let's start with hotel receptionists.

Sure. Last month I visited a hotel in the city centre, near the railway station. Receptionists welcome guests and help them check in. Their morning shift starts at half past seven. The hotel is called the Sunrise Hotel. Sunrise. That's S-U-N-R-I-S-E.
What skills do receptionists need?
They need to be polite, patient and organised. Speaking English is useful too, because the guests come from different countries.
Our second job is photographer.

Yes. I spoke to a photographer who takes pictures for families, shops and local events. She sometimes works in her studio, but she often travels to different places. She uses a camera, lights and a computer.
And finally, bus drivers.

I met a bus driver who starts work very early. His route goes through the city centre and past the hospital. One journey takes about fifty minutes. He likes meeting people and helping them get to work and school.
What do drivers need?
They need to be calm and careful, and they need the right driving licence.
If our listeners want advice about jobs, how can they contact you?
They can call our careers office. The number is oh two oh three, seven six eight, one four five.
Oh two oh three, seven six eight, one four five?
Yes, that's right. The office is open every weekday.
Thank you, Lucy. What's your best advice for young people?
Try different things, and remember that good communication and a positive attitude are useful in every job.
Hello, and welcome! Can I help you?
Yes, please. I'm looking for a present for my brother. I'll need a gift label with his name later. It's Oliver. That's O-L-I-V-E-R. It's his birthday next week.
Lovely! Does he like casual or formal clothes?
Casual. He likes simple jackets without bright colours.
This dark blue jacket is very popular. It's from a company called Kestrel. Kestrel. That's K-E-S-T-R-E-L.
It's nice, but it's a bit expensive. Do you have something cheaper?
This grey jacket costs thirty-five dollars. It's lighter, and it has two pockets outside and one small pocket inside.
Perfect. He always carries his phone and keys. I'll take it. Can I also buy a T-shirt?
Sure. We have white ones and green ones.
I'll take the green one. What if he doesn't like the clothes?
You can return or exchange them within thirty days, but you need the receipt.
OK. Can I pay by card?
Yes, of course. Would you like a gift bag?
Yes, please.
And if you ever want to check if we have your size, you can call us. Our number is oh one nine eight, two five four, seven three six.
Oh one nine eight, two five four, seven three six?
That's right. We're open every day until eight o'clock.
Great. Please write "Happy birthday! From your sister" on the label. And where's the exit?
Just go past the mirrors and turn left. Have a lovely day!
Good morning! How can I help?
Hi. I booked a seat on the train to Lakeside, but I can't find my ticket on my phone.
No problem. What's your surname?
Miller. That's M-I-L-L-E-R.
Here it is. You bought it online yesterday. Your seat is in coach C.
Great. Which platform does the train leave from?
Platform four. It leaves at nine twenty, and the journey takes about two hours.
Thanks. I'm visiting a friend in Lakeside. Is there a bus from the station to Rowan Street? Rowan. That's R-O-W-A-N.
Yes. The bus stops right outside the station café.
Perfect. Is there Wi-Fi on the train?
Yes, but the signal can be weak. There's also a café on the train where you can buy sandwiches and drinks.
Are there power sockets?
Only under some seats.
OK. My friend wants to show me a nature park, and she has a dog that loves walking by the water. I'm coming back on Sunday evening.
That sounds lovely. If you need help at Lakeside, call the station office. The number is oh one four four, nine two six, three five eight.
Oh one four four, nine two six, three five eight?
That's right. There's also a small shop next to Platform three. It sells snacks and newspapers. Please board the train through the front and middle doors, and don't leave your bags alone.
Thanks for your help! I'll buy a bottle of water first.
Welcome to Animal Friends! Today our guest is a young volunteer, Noah Reed. Noah, how do you spell your surname?
Reed. That's R-E-E-D.
How did you become interested in helping animals?
When I was ten, my family found a small dog near our home. He looked tired, and he didn't have a collar. We gave him some water and called an animal centre, and they found his owner.
Do you have a pet now?
Yes, a cat. She's three years old, and she has white and grey fur. She's very friendly, but she doesn't like loud noises.
Where do you volunteer?
At an animal centre that looks after dogs and cats that need new homes. I clean the animals' areas, prepare their food and take the dogs for walks.
Is there an animal you remember well?

Yes, a dog called Rocky. Rocky. That's R-O-C-K-Y. When he arrived, he was very nervous and stayed in a corner. We gave him time and treated him gently, and after a few weeks he started playing with the other dogs.
Did Rocky find a home?
Yes! In April, a family with two children and a large garden adopted him. A month later, they sent us a photo. He looked so happy.
How can people help?
They can volunteer, or give food and blankets. But please call before you visit. The number is oh two oh seven, seven four five, one nine three.
Oh two oh seven, seven four five, one nine three?
That's right.
Can children volunteer too?
Yes, from the age of twelve, with a parent.
Thank you, Noah!
Thank you. And remember, small acts of kindness can make a big difference.
Next week on Animal Friends, we're talking about horses.
Hello, and welcome to Everyday Choices, a podcast about simple habits that can make daily life better. I'm your presenter, Rachel Moore. Rachel is R-A-C-H-E-L, and Moore is M-O-O-R-E.
Today we're talking about healthy habits. Some people think a healthy lifestyle requires expensive food, special equipment or lots of free time. However, many useful habits are simple.

Let's begin with sleep. Having a regular sleeping routine can help you feel more organised. If you wake up at seven, you might choose to go to bed at around ten thirty or eleven. People need different amounts of sleep, but enough rest is important.

The second habit is drinking water. Some people forget to drink during busy days. One useful idea is to keep a bottle nearby. My bottle holds seven hundred and fifty millilitres. I fill it in the morning and take it to work.

Another habit is eating a variety of foods. Fruit, vegetables, grains and other foods can all be part of balanced meals. You don't need to eat the same thing every day. You could have eggs and bread for breakfast, rice with vegetables for lunch, and soup for dinner.

Movement is important too. You don't have to join a sports club. Walking, cycling, dancing and playing outside are all ways to move more. My neighbour, Thomas Hill, is a good example. Thomas is T-H-O-M-A-S, and Hill is H-I-L-L. He walks to work every day. His office is twenty-five minutes from his home.
It's also useful to take short breaks when studying. If you sit for a long time, stand up, stretch gently or walk around. Some people study for twenty-five minutes and then take a five-minute break.
Rest and enjoyable activities matter as well. Reading, listening to music and spending time with friends can help people relax.
Now, here's a message from Daniel in Brookfield. Brookfield is B-R-O-O-K-F-I-E-L-D. Daniel works from nine until five and often feels tired in the evening. He wants to become more active.
My suggestion is to start with a small change. Daniel could walk for ten minutes after lunch or take the stairs instead of the lift. He could also prepare a simple meal at home.

Remember, you don't need to change everything in one day. Choose one or two realistic goals and practise them regularly. A healthy lifestyle is built through small choices repeated over time. Thank you for listening to Everyday Choices.
Welcome to School Voices. Today's topic is technology. Our guests are Emily Parker and Jack Brown.
Emily is E-M-I-L-Y, and Parker is P-A-R-K-E-R.
Jack is J-A-C-K, and Brown is B-R-O-W-N.
Emily, how often do you use your phone?

Every day. I use it to message friends, check my school timetable, listen to music and find information. I also use a language-learning app for about fifteen minutes a day. Smartphones make life easier because I can contact my family and find directions. However, I sometimes watch too many short videos, so I put my phone away when studying.
Jack, what about you?

I use my laptop more than my phone because I do school projects on it. I also learn computer skills through free online lessons. I often use a website called Learn Online. Learn is L-E-A-R-N, and Online is O-N-L-I-N-E. It has short lessons about typing, presentations and spreadsheets. Some lessons are ten minutes long.
Do you use technology for entertainment?
Yes. I watch films, play games and listen to podcasts. But I try to finish homework first. Otherwise, I can lose track of time.
What should students remember about online safety?
Use strong passwords and avoid sharing private information with strangers. Think carefully before posting photographs or personal details.
Also, check information before believing or sharing it. Not everything online is correct. If I read an unusual story, I look for another reliable source.
Will technology change schools in the future?
Probably. Students may use more digital books and interactive lessons. Teachers can share materials online, which makes studying at home easier.
Technology will help teachers, but it won't replace them. Students still need people to explain difficult ideas and answer questions.
Emily, do you have a favourite device?
My favourite is my tablet, Nova. Nova is N-O-V-A. I use it to read and draw. I bought it last year for one hundred and eighty dollars.
Jack?
I like my wireless headphones. I bought them at Tech Corner. Tech is T-E-C-H, and Corner is C-O-R-N-E-R. The shop is at 42 Market Road. Market is M-A-R-K-E-T, and Road is R-O-A-D.

title: Behind the Scenes of a Movie

transcript.text: Welcome to Film Makers. Today we're speaking to a production assistant called Sophie Turner. Sophie is S-O-P-H-I-E, and Turner is T-U-R-N-E-R.
What does a production assistant do?

I help the film team organise daily work. I prepare schedules, check equipment, help actors find the correct places and communicate with different departments. It's busy because many people work together.
What film are you working on?
A family adventure film called The Secret Garden. The Secret is T-H-E, then S-E-C-R-E-T. Garden is G-A-R-D-E-N. It's about two children who discover an unusual garden near their grandmother's house.
Where are you filming?

Most scenes are filmed in Willow Creek. Willow is W-I-L-L-O-W, and Creek is C-R-E-E-K. It's about forty kilometres from the nearest large city. We also film indoor scenes at Studio North. Studio is S-T-U-D-I-O, and North is N-O-R-T-H.
How long does filming take?
About twelve weeks. After that, editors work on the film for several months. They choose the best scenes, add music, improve the sound and prepare the final version.
How many people are in the team?
About forty-five people, including the director, camera operators, actors, costume designers and sound assistants.
Tell us about the main actors.

The main character is played by Oliver James. Oliver is O-L-I-V-E-R, and James is J-A-M-E-S. He plays a boy called Leo. Leo is L-E-O. His sister is played by Hannah Price. Hannah is H-A-N-N-A-H, and Price is P-R-I-C-E.
Is there an animal in the film?
Yes, a small dog called Biscuit. Biscuit is B-I-S-C-U-I-T. He's friendly, but sometimes he doesn't follow instructions. We take a short break and try again.
When will the film be released?
The cinema release is planned for the eighteenth of December. The first trailer will come out on the fifth of October. The film will last about one hour and forty minutes.
What is the most difficult part of your job?
Keeping everything organised when the weather changes. If it rains during an outdoor scene, we may change the schedule and record an indoor scene instead.
What advice would you give someone interested in films?
Be organised, communicate clearly and be ready to learn. There are many jobs behind the camera, not only acting and directing.

title: Weather and Life Around the World

transcript.text: Welcome to World Weather Today. I'm your presenter, Laura Smith. Laura is L-A-U-R-A, and Smith is S-M-I-T-H. Today we're visiting four cities to find out how weather affects daily life.
Our first report comes from Oslo, the capital of Norway. Oslo is O-S-L-O. Our reporter is Erik Hansen. Erik is E-R-I-K, and Hansen is H-A-N-S-E-N.

Good morning from Oslo! It's a cold winter morning. The temperature is minus three degrees Celsius, and there is light snow. Many people are wearing warm coats, hats and gloves. The roads are slippery, so drivers are moving slowly. Some children have outdoor winter activities at school.
Thank you. Now let's travel to Nairobi in Kenya. Our reporter is Grace Mwangi. Grace is G-R-A-C-E, and Mwangi is M-W-A-N-G-I.

Hello from Nairobi! It's warm and sunny. The temperature is twenty-six degrees. Many people enjoy spending time outside. The rainy season is expected to begin next month, so people are preparing their gardens and checking their roofs.
Our next stop is Tokyo, Japan. Tokyo is T-O-K-Y-O. Our reporter is Kenji Sato. Kenji is K-E-N-J-I, and Sato is S-A-T-O.

Good afternoon from Tokyo. It's cloudy and eighteen degrees. There is a light wind, but no rain. The stations are busy because many people travel by train. In spring, Tokyo is famous for its cherry blossoms. Visitors go to parks to see the flowers and take photographs.
Finally, let's visit Sydney in Australia. Sydney is S-Y-D-N-E-Y. Our reporter is Mia Collins. Mia is M-I-A, and Collins is C-O-L-L-I-N-S.

Hello from Sydney! It's a bright summer day. The temperature is thirty-one degrees. Many people are going to the beach, swimming or having lunch outside. In summer, it can become very hot. People should drink water, use sun protection and look for shade during the hottest part of the day.
Thank you to all our reporters. Weather can be very different around the world. In one city, people may wear winter coats, while in another, they enjoy a sunny day at the beach.

Weather affects transport, school activities, work and travel plans. Before leaving home, it's useful to check the forecast and choose suitable clothes. Take an umbrella if rain is expected. Wear warm clothes in cold weather. On very hot days, drink enough water and avoid staying in the sun for too long.
